correctness.rationale: A complete rooted-multiset construction and collision-free tree-center canonicalization enumerate all unrooted trees through ten; adding every nonedge covers every simple connected unicyclic graph. Exhaustive bitmask enumeration proves the unique cycle maxima for \(3\le n\le10\). The 4-state transfer-matrix trace satisfies the verified characteristic cubic and yields \(c_{11}=486\), while conditioning on the attachment hub yields \(p_n=2^{n-2}+2n-2\) and \(p_{11}=532\). The displayed recurrence and induction prove p_n>c_n for all \(n\ge11\). The embedded standard-library certificate was executed and reproduced all claimed finite values. Noncomputational all-order steps are proved explicitly.

Its tree/path results do not establish the exhaustive uniqueness statement nor the infinite explicit nonoptimality family.

value.rationale: The 2026 counting study identifies a natural extremal counting invariant. Restricting to connected unicyclic graphs makes cycle maximality a mathematically motivated question distinct from its global tree extremum. This finding establishes a sharp first failure at n=11, proves unique cycle extremality at all earlier feasible orders through exhaustive complete graph generation, and gives a single concrete noncycle family beating the cycle for every larger order. The threshold is a natural first exception, and the proof connects a finite extremal census with an infinite transfer-matrix growth separation; no full global classification is claimed.
